STATUS: FINAL ENVIRONMENTAL STATEMENT
SUBJECT: KENDALL SQUARE
URBAN RENEWAL PROJECT
CAMBRIDGE, MASSACHUSETTS
HUD PROJECT NO. MASS. R-107
RESPONSIBLE FEDERAL AGENCY:
DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT BOSTON AREA OFFICE BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS
1. NAME OF ACTION: ADMINISTRATIVE.
2. BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE ACTION:
The Kendall Square Urban Renewal Project is located in the eastern part of the City of Cambridge and is close to the downtown area of Boston. The area is bounded by Binney Street to the north: Main Street to the south; Third Street to the east; and the Penn Central Railroad Tracks to the west.
The planned uses are light industry, technical and general office space, retail and consumer service stores, a fire station, residential, and a parking garage.
The purpose of this project is to complete development of an on-going urban renewal project approved in 1965 and centered around NASA. NASA withdrew from the project area, thus leaving the City of Cambridge with 44 acres of premdomintely cleared land. In September of 1974, HUD accepted an Amendatory Application to Urban Renewal Plan to allow the City to replan and complete the development of this area.
3. SUMMARY OF ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT AND ADVERSE ENVIRONMENTAL EFFECTS:
A. Positive Effects:
1. Eliminate blight.
2. Maximize the socio-economic potential of the project area with appropriate land uses and densities.
3. Promotes economic development to strengthen the City's tax base.
4. Improves visual aesthetics of the area.
5. Improves public utilities and vehicular movement in area.
6. Helps to stabilize the existing surrounding neighborhoods.
